105	## Manifests (`render.go`, `manifests/`)
106	
107	`Render(p Params) ([]byte, error)` calls `p.Validate()` first (an invalid value
108	returns Validate's error, naming its variable, and no bytes) and writes a
109	multi-document YAML stream separated by `---`, in this order: Namespace, PVC,
110	Deployment, Service. `RenderNamespace(p)` returns the first document alone, so
111	that `up` can apply the Namespace before the rest. The output is deterministic
112	(no map iteration, no timestamp); the golden of the defaults is
113	`testdata/render-default.golden.yaml`, rewritten with
114	`go test ./internal/nexusbench -run TestRenderGolden -update` and reviewed as a
115	diff.
116	
117	| File (`go:embed`, `text/template`) | Object |
118	|---|---|
119	| `00-namespace.yaml.tmpl` | Namespace, labels `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by` and `part-of` = `devdesk-nexus-bench`; no `pod-security.kubernetes.io/*` label |
120	| `10-pvc.yaml.tmpl` | PVC `nexus-data`, `ReadWriteOnce`, `StorageSize`, no `storageClassName` (the cluster default class, `local-path`) |
121	| `20-deployment.yaml.tmpl` | Deployment `nexus`: 1 replica, `Recreate`, one container (`ImageRef`), ports `http` 8081 and `docker-group` 8082, requests and limits, env `INSTALL4J_ADD_VM_PARAMS`, PVC on `/nexus-data`, `startupProbe` on `/service/rest/v1/status` (10 s x 60 = 10 min), `readinessProbe` (same path), no `livenessProbe`, UID and GID 200, `runAsNonRoot`, no privilege escalation, `drop: [ALL]`, `RuntimeDefault` seccomp, no service account token, no service links |
122	| `30-service.yaml.tmpl` | Service `nexus`, `NodePort`: `http` 8081 to `HTTPNodePort`, `docker-group` 8082 to `DockerNodePort` |
123	
124	Quoting: the templates see only a `manifestData` built from validated values,
125	and every string goes through the `q` template function (`strconv.Quote`, a
126	valid YAML double-quoted scalar), so `true`, `null`, `123`, `0x1F`, `12:30:45` or
127	`2001-01-23` in `NEXUS_BENCH_JVM_OPTS` decode as strings (`TestRenderRoundTripsTrickyJVMOpts`,
128	`TestRenderQuotesEveryValue`). Quoted: namespace, image reference, JVM options,
129	CPU and memory quantities, storage size. Not quoted: the two NodePorts (integers),
130	and the literals of the template (names, labels, container ports).
131	
132	What the render does not carry: the context, the upstream URL, `Anonymous`,
133	`AcceptEULA`, `Hosts`, timeouts and paths (a change of any of them leaves the
134	bytes unchanged, `TestRenderIgnoresParamsTheManifestsDoNotCarry`); no Secret, no
135	ConfigMap, no `envFrom` or `valueFrom`, no hostPath, no object of cluster scope
136	but the Namespace; the word `password` or `secret` never appears. The admin
137	password is read from the pod and written to the secrets file by the
138	provisioning step, not by a manifest.

140	## Errors, runner and preflight (`errors.go`, `kubectl.go`, `preflight.go`)
141	
142	**Errors.** Every failure of the bench is a `*BenchError{Kind, Cause, Check, Err}`.
143	`Error()` is `"<Cause>. Check: <Check>"`: a probable cause and what to run or look
144	at (a `kubectl` command, or a `mise` task), in English. `Err` is kept for
145	`errors.Is`/`errors.As` and is never printed: the text of a failed sub-process can
146	carry a credential, and neither the stderr of kubectl nor its error reaches a
147	message. `ErrKind` holds the kinds of D-F in the order the bench meets them:
148	`KubectlMissing`, `ContextNotFound`, `ClusterUnreachable`, `Forbidden`,
149	`NamespaceForeign`, `NamespaceMissing`, `NodePortTaken`, `AdmissionDenied`,
150	`PodPending`, `ImagePull`, `Crash`, `Deadline`, `RESTUnreachable`,
151	`ProvisionFailed`. The zero value is `Unclassified`, so an error nobody classified
152	never passes for a named kind. The last six are for the steps to come.
153	
154	`classifyKubectl(stderr)` is the fallback for what the exit status and the JSON
155	cannot tell apart; kubectl's wording changes between versions, so it matches
156	lower-cased fragments and returns `Unclassified` for an unknown text. Order of the
157	rules: an admission webhook that denied (even reported as `Forbidden`) is
158	`AdmissionDenied`; `provided port is already allocated` or `... not in the valid
159	range` is `NodePortTaken`; `forbidden` is `Forbidden`; `Unable to connect to the
160	server`, `connection refused`, `i/o timeout`, `TLS handshake timeout` are
161	`ClusterUnreachable`.
162	
163	**Runner.** `Runner.Run(ctx, stdin, args...)` returns both streams even on
164	failure. `NewExecRunner(context)` finds `kubectl` with `exec.LookPath` (a
165	`KubectlMissing` error otherwise, which names `kubectl` and `mise install`) and
166	puts `--context <context>` before every call, so callers never pass it.
167	`kubectl.go` is the only non-test file of the package that starts `kubectl`; the one other process is the `git check-ignore` of the secrets store (see below).
168	
169	**Preflight.** `RunPreflight(ctx, r, p, op) (PreflightResult, error)` with `op` one
170	of `OpUp`, `OpProvision`, `OpDown`, `OpStatus`. Checks, in this order, stopping at
171	the first failure:
172	
173	1. `p.Validate()`: invalid parameters are refused before any call.
174	2. `kubectl config get-contexts -o name`: the exact context name is listed, else
175	   `ContextNotFound`. Nothing else is asked.
176	3. `kubectl get --raw /readyz`: the API server answers, else `ClusterUnreachable`;
177	   a refusal (stderr `forbidden`: expired token, 403) is `Forbidden` instead, through
178	   the same `classifyKubectl` as every other call.
179	4. `kubectl auth can-i <verb> <resource>` (`-n <ns>`, `-A` or nothing):
180	   `up` needs create and patch `namespaces` (cluster; a server-side apply is a
181	   PATCH, also on a second run), create `persistentvolumeclaims`, `services`,
182	   `deployments` and `pods/exec` (namespace), list `services` (`-A`),
183	   patch `deployments`, `services` and `persistentvolumeclaims`, and get and list
184	   `pods` and `persistentvolumeclaims` (the wait of `Deploy`), all in the
185	   namespace (no manifest creates a Secret, so none is asked);
186	   `provision` needs create `pods/exec`, get `deployments` and list `pods`
187	   (namespace); `down` needs delete `namespaces`; `status`
188	   asks nothing. A `no` arrives on stdout with a non-zero exit, so stdout is read
189	   first: `Forbidden`, naming the verb and the resource.
190	5. `kubectl get namespace <ns> -o json`: absent is fine for `up` and `down` (nothing
191	   to delete) and `NamespaceMissing` for `provision` and `status`; present
192	   without the label `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=devdesk-nexus-bench` is
193	   `NamespaceForeign` for every operation (the plan lists `up` and `down`;
194	   `provision` and `status` refuse too, so the bench never runs `exec` in a
195	   namespace it did not create).
196	6. `up` only, `kubectl get services -A -o json`: a Service other than `nexus` of
197	   our namespace that holds `HTTPNodePort` or `DockerNodePort` is `NodePortTaken`,
198	   naming `<namespace>/<name>` and the port. Our own Service is accepted, which is
199	   what makes a second `up` possible.
200	7. Everything but `down`, `kubectl get nodes -o json`: `NodeIP` is the first
201	   `InternalIP`; none is not an error (`NodeIP` stays empty).
202	
203	A call that fails in a way the checks above did not expect goes through
204	`classifyKubectl` (a `forbidden` stderr becomes `Forbidden`, anything unknown
205	`Unclassified`). Every call that reaches the API server carries
206	`--request-timeout=10s`.
207	
208	**No write before the end of the preflight.** The preflight issues `config`,
209	`get` and `auth can-i` only, never sends stdin, and a failure at any point leaves
210	the cluster untouched. The tests run it against a scripted fake runner that fails
211	the test on any call outside the six above and records every write verb
212	(`apply`, `create`, `delete`, `patch`, `exec`, ...) it would have seen. The
213	`Runner` of the later steps (apply, delete) is only called after `RunPreflight`
214	returned without an error.

216	## Secrets and descriptor (`secrets.go`, `descriptor.go`)
217	
218	**Secrets.** `Secrets{AdminPassword, PendingAdminPassword, PullPassword}` (JSON
219	`adminPassword`, `pendingAdminPassword`, `pullPassword`; the last two are omitted
220	when empty) is kept by a `SecretStore` (`Load`, `Save`, `Remove`), implemented by
221	`NewFileStore(path)`. `PendingAdminPassword` is the new admin password, written
222	before it is sent to Nexus, so an interrupted change loses nothing.
223	
224	- Path: `DefaultSecretsPath(context, namespace, getenv)` is
225	  `$XDG_STATE_HOME/devdesk/nexus-bench/<context>/<namespace>/secrets.json`, else
226	  `$HOME/.local/state/...` (`USERPROFILE` when `HOME` is unset); an empty variable
227	  counts as unset, none of them set is an error, and `NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`
228	  overrides the whole path. It is outside every repository and shared by all the
229	  worktrees, so a worktree never keeps a stale admin password of its own.
230	- Modes: the file is `0600`, the folders `Save` creates are `0700`. The write is
231	  atomic (`writeFileAtomic`): a temporary file in the same folder, `chmod`, sync,
232	  rename, then a best-effort sync of the folder so the new name survives a power
233	  cut (errors ignored: Windows and some file systems cannot sync a folder); the
234	  temporary file is removed when anything fails, so a failed `Save`
235	  leaves no partial file and a file left by someone else with a wider mode is
236	  replaced, not kept. POSIX modes are not meaningful on Windows (the test skips).
237	- File name: `NewFileStore` refuses a path whose file name is not `secrets.json`
238	  (`Remove` deletes that file, and a mistyped `NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS` must not point
239	  it at `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`).
240	- Mode on read: `Load` refuses a file with a group or other bit (`mode & 0o077`),
241	  outside Windows, with a `BenchError` that never shows the content and says
242	  `chmod 600 <path>`.
243	- Display: `Secrets` has `String`, `GoString` and `LogValue` methods that all give
244	  `Secrets{redacted}`, so no fmt verb (`%v`, `%+v`, `%#v`, `%s`, `%q`) and no slog
245	  handler prints a password (`TestSecretsAreRedactedWhenFormatted`). The JSON of
246	  the file is unaffected.
247	- `Load` returns `(zero, false, nil)` when the file is absent. A file that is not a
248	  valid JSON object is a `BenchError` that names the path and never shows the
249	  content (the underlying error is kept in `Err`, which is not printed).
250	- `Remove` deletes the file, then the namespace folder when it is empty; it
251	  succeeds when there is nothing to remove, and a folder holding anything else
252	  stays.
253	- Git guard: `NewFileStore` refuses an empty path and touches nothing on disk.
254	  It walks up from the file's folder looking for a `.git` entry (directory or
255	  file, so a worktree counts); with none, the path is accepted without asking
256	  git. With one, it runs `git -C <root> check-ignore -q -- <path>`: ignored is
257	  accepted; not ignored, or git unavailable, is a `BenchError` that says to set
258	  `NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS` outside the repository. The process runs with the caller's
259	  environment minus `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`,
260	  `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_NAMESPACE`, `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`,
261	  `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*`,
262	  `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_*`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` and
263	  `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` (`gitEnvironment`), then `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=<devnull>` and
264	  `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, so the verdict is about the repository of the path and
265	  its own ignore rules, not about a repository or a `core.excludesFile` the
266	  caller's variables or configuration point at (a path ignored only by a global
267	  excludes file is therefore refused). That call is the only process
268	  outside `kubectl.go`; it lives in the package variable `gitIgnores`, so it can
269	  be replaced and found by a source guard.
270	
271	**Descriptor.** `BuildDescriptor(p, DeployResult, ProvisionResult)` returns the
272	`Descriptor` of schema 1 (D-D): `schemaVersion`, `kubeContext`, `namespace`,
273	`image`, `nexusVersion`, `edition`, `eulaAccepted`, `hosts`, `rest`,
274	`dockerConnectors`, `repositories`, `realms`, `accounts`, in that order, which is the
275	order of the struct fields. `hosts` is `Params.Hosts` when set, else `127.0.0.1`
276	then `DeployResult.NodeIP` when it is not empty; the URLs are `http://<host>:<nodePort>`
277	for each host (`RESTBaseURL(host, p)` is the exported REST origin: brackets for
278	IPv6, `%25` for a zone; the deployment, the descriptor and the command of step 8
279	all build it there). `DeployResult{ReachableHosts, NodeIP}` (step 4) and
280	`ProvisionResult{NexusVersion, Edition, EULAAccepted}` (step 6) are defined in
281	`descriptor.go` and reused by those steps. The account `anonymous` always
282	appears; its `enabled` is a `*bool`, so `false` is written when
283	`NEXUS_BENCH_ANONYMOUS=false`, and the other accounts write no `enabled`.
284	
285	- `WriteDescriptor(path, d)`: JSON indented by two spaces, one final newline, `0644`
286	  file, atomic through the same helper; the bytes depend on `d` alone.
287	- `LoadDescriptor(path)`: a missing file is `ErrNoDescriptor` (wrapped, use
288	  `errors.Is`); invalid JSON or a `schemaVersion` other than 1 (missing counts as 0)
289	  is an error that names the file and never shows its content.
290	- `DescriptorPath()`: `NEXUS_BENCH_DESCRIPTOR` when set and not empty, else
291	  `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json`, found with `runtime.Caller`, so it does
292	  not depend on the working directory (and does not survive `-trimpath`).
293	- Never in the descriptor: a password or any secret, the path of the secrets file,
294	  a timestamp, a pod name, or the word `password` (`TestDescriptorHoldsNoSecret`,
295	  `TestDescriptorFormat`).
296	
297	The golden `testdata/descriptor.example.json` is the descriptor of `Defaults()`
298	with node IP `192.168.1.31`, Nexus `3.98.1-01`, `COMMUNITY`, EULA accepted. It is
299	checked both ways: `WriteDescriptor` must write exactly these bytes
300	(`TestDescriptorGolden`) and `LoadDescriptor` must read back `BuildDescriptor`'s
301	value (`TestLoadDescriptorGoldenMatchesBuild`). After a deliberate change of the
302	schema, regenerate it with
303	`go test ./internal/nexusbench -run TestDescriptorGolden -update` and review the
304	diff by hand (bump `schemaVersion` when a field changes meaning).

306	## REST client and provisioning (`nexusapi.go`, `provision.go`, `initialpassword.go`)
307	
308	`Provision(ctx, baseURL, ip, store, p, out) (ProvisionResult, error)` brings a
309	running Nexus to the state the bench needs (D-E). `baseURL` is the REST origin
310	(no path); `ip` is an `InitialPassword` (`Read(ctx) (pw, ok, err)`); `out` gets
311	progress lines (`provision: ...`) and never a password.
312	
313	**Idempotence.** Every object is read, then created when absent or replaced when
314	present; there is no "create and ignore the error". A second run sends no `POST`
315	(except the one `POST` of a proxy whose upstream does not resolve yet, see
316	"Unresolvable upstream" under call 9 below) and changes neither the state nor
317	any password. Order of the calls:
318	
319	1. `GET /v1/status` (no account): version and edition from the `Server` header
320	   (`Nexus/3.98.1-01 (COMMUNITY)`), else `info.version` of
321	   `/service/rest/swagger.json`, else empty (a note on `out`). The version is
322	   optional: a swagger answer that is a refusal or not JSON (a proxy page) leaves
323	   it empty; only a transport failure stops the run.
324	2. Admin credentials (below).
325	3. EULA: `GET /v1/system/eula`; 404 means an edition without one (noted,
326	   `EULAAccepted` false); `accepted: true` changes nothing; otherwise it is
327	   accepted only when `Params.AcceptEULA` (`NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA=yes`), with
328	   `POST {"accepted":true,"disclaimer":<as received>}`; the disclaimer is kept as
329	   a `json.RawMessage`, never rebuilt. Without consent `Provision` stops with a
330	   `ProvisionFailed` that names `NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA` and says that no
331	   repository, role or account was created, before any creation (the
332	   only write before it is the admin password change, which the EULA read needs).
333	4. Blob store: `GET /v1/blobstores` must list `default`, else `ProvisionFailed`
334	   before any role, user or repository is created.
335	5. Realms: `GET /v1/security/realms/active`; the missing ones of
336	   `NexusAuthenticatingRealm`, `DockerToken` are appended and the list is
337	   `PUT` back (a list that is already complete is not written). The plan said
338	   "set these two"; appending keeps a realm the instance already needs.
339	6. Anonymous access: `GET`, then always `PUT {"enabled": Params.Anonymous,
340	   "userId": "anonymous", "realmName": <current, default NexusAuthorizingRealm>}`.
341	7. Role `bench-docker-pull` (`nx-repository-view-docker-*-browse` and `-read`):
342	   `GET` 404 then `POST`, found then `PUT`.
343	8. User `bench-pull` (role above, status `active`): `GET /users?userId=bench-pull`,
344	   then `POST` with the password, or `PUT` plus `PUT .../change-password` with the
345	   stored password. The list filter matches by substring, so the element whose
346	   `userId` is exactly `bench-pull` is the one used.
347	9. `docker-hosted`, `docker-proxy` (`remoteUrl` = `Params.UpstreamURL`,
348	   `indexType: REGISTRY`) and `docker-group` (members hosted then proxy,
349	   `docker.httpPort: 8082`), all on blob store `default`, `forceBasicAuth: false`
350	   (anonymous pulls): `GET .../{name}` 404 then `POST`, found then `PUT`.
351	   **Unresolvable upstream.** Nexus resolves the host of the proxy's remote URL
352	   when it saves the repository and answers `400` (validation error on
353	   `proxy.remoteUrl`) when it does not. The client keeps one verdict from that
354	   answer, `APIError.RemoteURLBlocked` (a boolean, true only for a `400` with an
355	   entry whose id ends in `proxy.remoteUrl` and whose message contains `resolve
356	   host`, case-insensitive, in a body of at most 4 KiB; the body is parsed and
357	   dropped, no text of it is kept or printed; a malformed URL or any other
358	   refusal of that field is an ordinary failure). On that verdict `Provision`
359	   writes `provision: warning: Nexus refused the remote URL of docker-proxy: it
360	   cannot resolve the upstream host yet, so it was left out; run up again once
361	   the upstream exists`, goes on, creates the group with `docker-hosted` as its only
362	   member, and returns `ProvisionResult.ProxyPending` (true only when the proxy
363	   does not exist; an existing proxy stays, stays a member, and the warning says
364	   `left as it was`). Any other `400`, or a `400` on another repository, still
365	   fails. `BuildDescriptor` then lists neither `docker-proxy` nor it as a group
366	   member. A run after NX-02 deployed the upstream creates the proxy and updates
367	   the group, and the descriptor changes (commit it). So a second `up` is not
368	   POST-free while the proxy is pending: it sends the one refused `POST` of the
369	   proxy.
370	
371	**Admin credentials, a state machine with the write first.** `Load` the store;
372	the candidates are `adminPassword`, then `pendingAdminPassword`; an empty value
373	is never tried (a `{}` file means "not provided", and no request carries an empty
374	password). A candidate is accepted when `GET /v1/security/users?userId=admin`
375	answers 2xx; a 401 is a refusal and goes to the next candidate, any other status
376	is an error (a redirect or a 500 is not "wrong password"). A pending password
377	that the instance accepts is promoted to `adminPassword` with no new change.
378	When no candidate works, `InitialPassword.Read` supplies the password of the pod:
379	absent or refused gives the error `the bench admin password is unknown ...`, with
380	the check `mise run nexus-bench:down`, then `up`. Otherwise a password is
381	generated (or the stored pending one is reused), **`Save` stores it as
382	`pendingAdminPassword` first**, then `PUT /users/admin/change-password`
383	(`text/plain`) runs with the initial password, then `Save` promotes it to
384	`adminPassword`. A failed `Save` stops the run before the instance is touched
385	(`TestProvisionStopsWhenSaveFails`); a crash between the steps is resumed from the
386	pending password on the next run. The pull password follows the same rule: stored
387	before the user is created or its password set.
388	
389	**Generated passwords** are 32 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9]` from `crypto/rand`
390	(rejection sampling, no modulo bias), never a fixed or predictable value.
391	
392	**`kubectlInitialPassword`** (`NewKubectlInitialPassword(runner, namespace)`) runs
393	`-n <ns> exec deploy/nexus -- cat /nexus-data/admin.password` through the
394	`Runner`, so `kubectl.go` stays the only file that starts a process. A "No such
395	file or directory" on stderr is (empty, false, nil); another failure is a
396	`BenchError` (kind from `classifyKubectl`, else `ProvisionFailed`) whose message
397	holds neither stdout nor stderr. Unit-tested on a fake `Runner`; no integration
398	test.
399	
400	**Client** (`client`, `newClient(baseURL, user, password)`): a dedicated
401	`http.Client` with `Timeout` 15 s, no proxy (the environment's proxy would receive
402	the credentials), and a `CheckRedirect` that returns `http.ErrUseLastResponse`:
403	no redirection is followed, so the 3xx is the answer and the target is never
404	contacted or named. A 2xx answer is read through `io.LimitReader` at 1 MiB + 1;
405	more is a `tooLargeError` and the content is never decoded (exactly 1 MiB is
406	read). Basic auth is set per request, only when there is a user; no header is
407	logged.
408	
409	**Errors.** `*APIError{Op, Status}` prints `<Op>: HTTP <status> <text>`: no URL,
410	no request or answer body. `Provision` returns `*BenchError` only:
411	`RESTUnreachable` when a call got no answer, `ProvisionFailed` otherwise, with
412	the `*APIError` (or the store or pod error) in `Err` so `errors.As` and
413	`errors.Is` reach it. A 401 or 403 adds the hint that the stored admin password
414	may not match. No error and no line on `out` holds a password
415	(`TestProvisionNeverPrintsAPassword`, and `requireQuiet` after every scenario,
416	which knows every password the fake saw).
417	
418	**H-REST: unverified hypotheses.** The in-memory Nexus of `fakenexus_test.go`
419	(`httptest`, loopback) is the one place that knows the JSON shapes, and it was
420	written from the Sonatype documentation, not from an instance. To check against
421	`/service/rest/swagger.json` at step 10, and to fix in the fake and the client
422	together:
423	
424	- the `Server` header on `/v1/status`, and the swagger fallback;
425	- the EULA payload and the `404` of an edition without one;
426	- `change-password` as `text/plain`, and whether `admin.password` is deleted once
427	  the password is changed through the API;
428	- the realm ids (`DockerToken`) and that the active list can be read and `PUT`;
429	- the anonymous payload (`enabled`, `userId`, `realmName`);
430	- the role and user payloads (`source` only on `PUT`, `externalRoles`), and a
431	  `userId` filter that matches by substring;
432	- the repository payloads (`storage`, `docker`, `proxy`, `dockerProxy`,
433	  `negativeCache`, `httpClient`, `group.memberNames`, `docker.httpPort`), the
434	  statuses of `POST` (201) and `PUT` (204), the path-routing field added in 3.83
435	  (left to the default of Nexus), and a proxy created before its upstream exists.
436	
437	Verdict of the first real run (details in "First real run"): every item above
438	held except the last one. The `Server` header, the EULA payload, `text/plain`
439	change-password, the realm ids, the anonymous, role, user and repository
440	payloads and all the statuses matched the swagger and the fake. A proxy created
441	before its upstream resolves is refused with `400`; the fake does the same since
442	(`BlockUpstream`, `ResolveUpstream`).
443	
444	**Security guarantees.** No redirect followed; answers bounded; no proxy; no
445	`Authorization` header, URL with credentials, body or password in any error or
446	output; passwords written to the store before use; an empty password never sent;
447	no process started outside `kubectl.go`.

449	## Destruction and the clock (`destroy.go`, `clock.go`)
450	
451	`Destroy(ctx, runner, clock, store, params, out)` is the one irreversible
452	operation of the bench (risk R1), so its order is fixed:
453	
454	1. `RunPreflight(OpDown)`: `Validate` first (no call at all), then context,
455	   `/readyz`, `auth can-i delete namespaces`, and the namespace. A namespace
456	   without the label `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=devdesk-nexus-bench` is
457	   refused here with `NamespaceForeign`, before any write.
458	2. A namespace that is absent prints `nothing to delete` and succeeds. The
459	   stored secrets are removed anyway, so a stale `secrets.json` does not
460	   outlive its bench and a second `down` is idempotent.
461	3. **One write**: `delete namespace <ns> --wait=false`, issued once, never
462	   retried (a `Forbidden` is returned as is). Nothing else is ever written: no
463	   finalizer patch, no force delete, no delete of another object. The tests
464	   journal every call and fail on a second write.
465	4. The namespace is read (`get namespace <ns> -o json`) until `NotFound` or
466	   `NEXUS_BENCH_DELETE_TIMEOUT` (default 3 min). The first read is immediate; the
467	   interval between reads doubles from 1 s to 10 s, always through `Clock.Sleep`
468	   and clipped to what remains of the timeout. A namespace stuck in `Terminating`
469	   ends in a `Deadline` error that cites the namespace, `spec.finalizers` and
470	   each `status.conditions` entry (type, status, message); the bench does not
471	   remove them.
472	5. One read of `get pv -o json`. A PersistentVolume whose `claimRef.namespace` is
473	   the bench namespace prints a line starting with `warning:` that names it and
474	   its phase and says it still exists: the run still succeeds, because the
475	   reclaim policy decides (`Delete` may remove it seconds later, `Retain` keeps
476	   the data on the node) and the bench does not delete a volume itself. No such volume, no
477	   warning. A PV list that cannot be read is also a warning, not a failure.
478	6. `store.Remove()`, last, and only when the namespace is gone. Its failure is
479	   returned as a `BenchError` (the namespace is already deleted; running `down`
480	   again retries the removal). A failed or cancelled run never touches the
481	   secrets.
482	
483	A cancelled context ends the wait with an error that wraps `context.Canceled`
484	(`errors.Is` holds); the namespace keeps terminating on the cluster. Lines on
485	`out` start with `down:` and, like every error, hold no password.
486	
487	`Clock` (`Now`, `Sleep(ctx, d) error`) is how the waits spend time. `NewClock()`
488	is the wall clock: `Sleep` returns `ctx.Err()` when the context is done (before
489	sleeping, even for a zero duration), returns at once for `d <= 0`, and otherwise
490	waits on a timer or the context. `fakeClock` of `clock_test.go` moves its time
491	forward instead of waiting, so no test sleeps for real.
492	
493	## Deployment and the wait (`deploy.go`, `probe.go`)
494	
495	`Deploy(ctx, runner, prober, clock, params, out) (DeployResult, error)` applies
496	the manifests and waits until Nexus answers. Order, fixed:
497	
498	1. `RunPreflight(OpUp)`, whole; no write before it succeeds.
499	2. `ctx` is looked at (a runner may ignore it), then
500	   `kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager=devdesk-nexus-bench -f -` with
501	   `RenderNamespace(p)` on stdin: the Namespace alone, so a failure later leaves
502	   at worst our labeled namespace and never anything outside it.
503	3. The same apply with `Render(p)`: the whole stream, the Namespace again
504	   included. A second `up` sends the same two applies and gets the same result;
505	   `--prune` is never used.
506	4. The wait, one round per `pollInterval` (5 s) through `Clock.Sleep`: read
507	   `get pods -n <ns> -l app.kubernetes.io/name=nexus -o json` and
508	   `get pvc -n <ns> -o json`, diagnose them, then probe every host. The deadline
509	   is `NEXUS_BENCH_TIMEOUT` (10 min); it is checked after a round, so the cluster
510	   is read once more at the very end.
511	
512	**Failure of an apply** is classified from its stderr by `classifyKubectl`:
513	`NodePortTaken` (names `NEXUS_BENCH_HTTP_NODEPORT` and `..._DOCKER_NODEPORT`),
514	`AdmissionDenied` (a webhook refusal wins over the `Forbidden` the API server
515	also reports), `Forbidden`, `ClusterUnreachable`, else `Unclassified`. The
516	runner's error is the `Err` of the `BenchError` (for `errors.Is`); neither the
517	stderr nor the error of the prober is ever in a message. After a failed apply
518	nothing else is called: no read, no probe, no sleep.
519	
520	**Diagnosis**, each round, on the pods that are not being deleted:
521	
522	| Reading | Kind | When |
523	|---|---|---|
524	| container waiting on `ErrImagePull` or `ImagePullBackOff` | `ImagePull` (names the image and `NEXUS_BENCH_IMAGE`, `_IMAGE_TAG`) | at once |
525	| `CrashLoopBackOff`, or `OOMKilled` as last or current termination | `Crash` (names the memory limit and `NEXUS_BENCH_MEMORY_LIMIT`) | at once |
526	| `PodScheduled=False`, reason `Unschedulable`, message with `Insufficient memory` or `Insufficient cpu` | `PodPending` (the request and `NEXUS_BENCH_MEMORY_REQUEST` or `_CPU_REQUEST`) | after `pendingGrace` (30 s) |
527	| claim `Pending` while a pod is scheduled | `PodPending` (the size and `NEXUS_BENCH_STORAGE_SIZE`) | after `pendingGrace` |
528	| no host answers by the deadline | `Deadline` (last state of the pod and the claim, the hosts tried, `NEXUS_BENCH_TIMEOUT`) | at `Params.Timeout` |
529	
530	The unschedulable pod is read before the claim: while the pod is not scheduled, a
531	claim of a `WaitForFirstConsumer` class is `Pending` for that reason alone and is
532	not blamed. A reading that changes or disappears restarts the grace count (the
533	volume binds when the pod is scheduled; the Deployment may have made no pod yet).
534	When the deadline arrives with such a reading still active, it is returned as
535	`PodPending` rather than `Deadline`. A cancelled context is returned as is
536	(`errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)`), never as a `Deadline`.
537	
538	**Reached hosts.** The hosts are `Params.Hosts` when set, else `127.0.0.1` and
539	the node `InternalIP` (when there is one). Each round probes them in parallel at
540	`http://<host>:<HTTPNodePort>` (`net.JoinHostPort`, so IPv6 gets brackets) and
541	returns after the first round in which at least one answered, with
542	`DeployResult.ReachableHosts` = the hosts that answered in that round, in host
543	order. A host that did not answer then gets a line on `out` that starts with
544	`deploy: warning:` and names it; no warning when all answered. `BuildDescriptor`
545	lists in `hosts` (and in every URL) `Params.Hosts` when set, else
546	`ReachableHosts` when not empty, else the earlier fallback (`127.0.0.1` and
547	`NodeIP`), so the descriptor never promises a host that did not answer
548	(`descriptor_hosts_test.go`).
549	
550	**Prober** (`probe.go`): `NewProber()` is one unauthenticated `GET
551	<baseURL>/service/rest/v1/status` on a dedicated client (5 s timeout, no proxy,
552	no keep-alive, `CheckRedirect` returning `http.ErrUseLastResponse`): nil on 200
553	and only then, otherwise a `*APIError` (status only) or a `*transportError`
554	(wrapping the cause for `errors.Is`). The body is neither read for its content
555	nor reported, and a redirect target is never contacted.
556	
557	**Rights the deployment needs** (all asked by the preflight, namespace-scoped
558	except the first two): create and patch `namespaces` (cluster); create and patch
559	`persistentvolumeclaims`, `services`, `deployments`; get and list `pods` and
560	`persistentvolumeclaims`; create `pods/exec` (used by `Provision`); list `services` in all namespaces (NodePort check).
561	
562	**Not covered by the fakes.** `Deploy` has only run against a scripted `Runner`,
563	a fake `Prober` and a fake `Clock`; the real kubectl output shape of
564	`get pods -o json` (container status fields), the real duration of the pull and
565	the start, and whether `kubectl apply --server-side` of a Namespace that carries
566	no field of its own conflicts on a second run were left for step 10: the real
567	output was read, a second `up` applied the same two documents with no conflict,
568	and the start took 48 s (see "First real run").
569	
570	## Residual risks (security audit of the steps 4, 6, 7)
571	
572	Known and accepted for a throw-away bench; none is fixed by this change.
573	
574	- **Basic credentials in clear HTTP.** Nexus is reached on `http://`, so the admin
575	  and `bench-pull` credentials of `Provision` travel unencrypted. The command
576	  honours the commitment made for it: it sends them to
577	  `RESTBaseURL("127.0.0.1", p)` and to another host only on `--rest-host`, with a
578	  warning (see "The command"). The package itself does not enforce it.
579	- **`local-path` volume in `0777`.** The data folder of the local-path
580	  provisioner is world-writable, so `admin.password` is readable by every local
581	  account of the node between the start of Nexus and the provisioning (which
582	  changes it).
583	- **NodePorts on the LAN, anonymous access on purpose.** The two NodePorts listen
584	  on every interface of the node, and anonymous access is enabled by default so
585	  that pulls need no login (`NEXUS_BENCH_ANONYMOUS`). Anyone on the LAN can read
586	  the bench; do not put anything private in it.
587	- **Mutable image tag.** The image is `docker.io/sonatype/nexus3:<tag>` with no
588	  digest: the same tag can resolve to another image later.
589	- **Partial result on error.** `Provision` returns the `ProvisionResult` it had
590	  gathered together with the error. The command does not write the descriptor
591	  when `err != nil` (`TestDescriptorIsNotWrittenUnlessProvisionSucceeded`), or it
592	  would describe a bench that is half provisioned.

594	## The command and the mise tasks (`cmd/nexus-bench`, `mise.toml`)
595	
596	`internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench` is a `package main` of five files:
597	`main.go` (`deps`, `defaultDeps`, `run`), `flags.go` (flags and parameter
598	resolution), `commands.go` (`up`, `provision`, `down`, `render`), `status.go` and
599	`usage.go` (the help). `main()` only builds a context cancelled by SIGINT and
600	SIGTERM, calls `run(ctx, args, os.Getenv, os.Stdout, os.Stderr, defaultDeps())`
601	and exits with its code. `deps` holds every constructor and library call that
602	reaches a cluster (`newRunner`, `newProber`, `clock`, `newStore`, `newInitial`,
603	`preflight`, `deploy`, `provision`, `destroy`); `defaultDeps` wires
604	`NewExecRunner`, `NewProber`, `NewClock`, `NewFileStore`,
605	`NewKubectlInitialPassword`, `RunPreflight`, `Deploy`, `Provision` and `Destroy`,
606	and the tests wire fakes, so no test needs kubectl or a network.
607	
608	**Tasks.** Six, in `mise.toml`, none reachable from `ci`, `check`, `test` or
609	`test-race` (`mise_tasks_test.go` reads the file and checks it, and checks that
610	`kubectl` is declared on each of them, not in the global `[tools]`, so the CI does
611	not install it; kubectl `1.35`, because `datomir` runs k0s v1.36.x and kubectl is
612	supported within one minor version of the API server, so 1.35 is the oldest
613	accepted; `render` contacts no cluster and declares no kubectl, and the test
614	requires its absence there). Arguments follow `--`: mise appends them to the
615	command line.
616	
617	| Task | Runs | Acts on the cluster |
618	|---|---|---|
619	| `nexus-bench:up` | `go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench up` | yes |
620	| `nexus-bench:provision` | `... provision` | yes (REST and `exec`) |
621	| `nexus-bench:down` | `... down` | yes (deletes the namespace) |
622	| `nexus-bench:status` | `... status` | reads only |
623	| `nexus-bench:render` | `... render` | no, contacts nothing |
624	| `nexus-bench:test` | `go test -timeout 60m -count=1 -run Integration ./internal/nexusbench/...` with `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1` set by the task's `env` table (portable, no `env` command) | yes; the tests skip when `CI` is set |
625	
626	**Subcommands and flags.** Every subcommand takes the same parameter flags, one
627	per `NEXUS_BENCH_*` variable: `--context`, `--namespace`, `--http-nodeport`,
628	`--docker-nodeport`, `--cpu-request`, `--cpu-limit`, `--memory-request`,
629	`--memory-limit`, `--storage-size`, `--jvm-opts`, `--image`, `--image-tag`,
630	`--upstream-url`, `--anonymous`, `--hosts`, `--timeout`, `--delete-timeout`,
631	`--secrets`, `--descriptor`. `up` and `provision` add `--accept-eula` and
632	`--rest-host`. Each subcommand has its own `flag.FlagSet` (`ContinueOnError`,
633	output discarded: the command prints parse errors itself on stderr and `-h` on
634	stdout). A flag is laid over its variable and the result goes through
635	`FromEnv(Defaults(), ...)` once, so "flag, then `NEXUS_BENCH_*`, then default",
636	the parsing and the rule that `--namespace` moves the upstream URL (unless an
637	upstream is given, by flag or variable) are the library's own. `--accept-eula`
638	becomes `yes` (and `--accept-eula=false` `no`, which beats a variable set to
639	`yes`). `Validate` runs before anything else, `render` included.
640	
641	**Exit codes.** `0` success; `1` failure (invalid parameter, kubectl missing, a
642	step failed, a run cancelled); `2` mistake in the command line (no or unknown
643	subcommand, unknown flag, a value of the wrong type, a missing value, an extra
644	argument), with the help on stderr when the subcommand is missing or unknown.
645	`help`, `-h` and `--help` print on stdout and exit `0`. `go run` (so every
646	`mise run nexus-bench:*`) does not propagate the code: it prints `exit status 2`
647	and exits `1`. Code `2` is only visible when the compiled binary is run directly;
648	the general help says so (`TestHelpSaysGoRunDoesNotKeepExitCodeTwo`).
649	
650	**Interruption.** `main()` cancels the run's context on SIGINT or SIGTERM and
651	then hands the signals back to the default behavior (`context.AfterFunc(ctx,
652	stop)`), so a second Ctrl-C kills a run that is slow to wind down. This is not
653	unit-tested: it lives in `main()`, which the tests do not call.
654	
655	**Output.** The progress of the library steps goes to stdout, then one line
656	`nexus-bench: descriptor written to <path>`. Every failure is one line on stderr:
657	a `BenchError` (also when wrapped by `%w` or joined) prints exactly its
658	`Error()`, and nothing around it or inside it (no wrapper text, no `Err`, no
659	trace); a cancelled run says `cancelled` and that `status` shows where things
660	stand; another error prints its message. No output holds a password
661	(`requireClean` of the tests plants markers in the fakes).
662	
663	**`up`.** Resolve the parameters, then the secrets path
664	(`--secrets`/`NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`, else `DefaultSecretsPath`; with no place for
665	it the run stops before any cluster call and says to set
666	`NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`), `newRunner`, `newStore` (the git guard), `Deploy` (which
667	runs `RunPreflight(OpUp)` itself, so the command does not run a second one), then
668	`Provision`, then the descriptor. **The descriptor is written only after a
669	successful `Provision`**, never on a failure at any step, and a descriptor from
670	an earlier run is left as it was. It is built with `BuildDescriptor(p,
671	DeployResult, ProvisionResult)`.
672	
673	**`provision`.** `RunPreflight(OpProvision)`, `Provision`, then the descriptor,
674	built with `DeployResult{NodeIP: <node address of the preflight>}`.
675	
676	**`down`.** `Destroy` (its own `RunPreflight(OpDown)` first). The descriptor is
677	not touched or created.
678	
679	**`status`.** Read-only: `RunPreflight(OpStatus)` (a missing namespace is its
680	`NamespaceMissing` error, exit `1`), one `kubectl get pods -l
681	app.kubernetes.io/name=nexus -o json`, one probe of the REST origin, one read of
682	the descriptor. Four lines, each a finding, exit `0`:
683	
684	    bench: namespace nexus-bench, context datomir
685	    pod: running (nexus-xxx, 1/1 ready, 0 restarts)     | not found | pending ...
686	    rest: ready (http://127.0.0.1:30481)                 | not ready (the cause is not shown)
687	    descriptor: matches (<path>) | not found (<path>) | differs from the current parameters (<path>) + one line per field
688	
689	The comparison covers context, namespace, image, both NodePorts, the upstream URL
690	and the anonymous flag; hosts and versions come from the cluster and are left out.
691	It creates no store, builds no `InitialPassword` and sends no credential.
692	
693	**`render`.** Prints `Render(p)` and nothing else; it builds no dependency (the
694	test runs it with an empty `deps`).
695	
696	**Where the credentials go.** `Provision` is given
697	`RESTBaseURL("127.0.0.1", p)`, whatever hosts `Deploy` reached, so the admin and
698	`bench-pull` passwords stay on the loopback by default. `--rest-host <host>`
699	(a host name, an IPv4 or IPv6 address, brackets and a zone allowed; no port,
700	scheme, path, credentials or space, refused before any cluster call with exit
701	`1`) sends them to that host instead, and unless it is a loopback address or
702	`localhost` the command prints on stderr a warning that the credentials travel in
703	clear text. `status` and the deployment wait probe without credentials.
704	
705	**Non-default bench.** After writing the descriptor, if the parameters differ
706	from `Defaults()` (any field but the two timeouts, the two paths, the EULA
707	consent and an empty host list), stderr gets `warning: descriptor.json now
708	describes a non-default bench; do not commit it`. The file is written all the
709	same, at `--descriptor`/`NEXUS_BENCH_DESCRIPTOR`, else the versioned one. A
710	default bench prints nothing on stderr.

712	## Integration tests and source guards (`bench_integration_test.go`, `guard_test.go`, step 9)
713	
714	Read-only state of the run on 2026-11-16: the three read tests pass (8 subtests)
715	and the lifecycle passes (151 s for two downs and three deployments).

717	**Gates.** Every test of `bench_integration_test.go` starts with
718	`requireBench(t)`: it skips unless `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1` and `CI` is empty, so

726	(`mise run nexus-bench:up`): they read the versioned descriptor and the secrets

730	| Test | Reads | Writes |
731	|---|---|---|
732	| `TestIntegrationBenchDescribed` | `GET /service/rest/v1/status` without credentials (200), then as admin the repository list and, per repository of the descriptor, its type, format, group members or proxy remote URL | nothing |

776	2. *Only `kubectl.go` and `secrets.go` start a process* (`exec.Command` or
777	   `CommandContext`, any import name, dot import refused): one door to the
778	   cluster, one to `git check-ignore`. A listed file that no longer starts one
779	   must be dropped from the list. Limit: `syscall.Exec`, `os.StartProcess` and a
780	   process started by another package are not seen.
781	3. *No Authorization header outside the client.* The word `authorization` (in an
782	   identifier or a string) may appear only in `nexusapi.go` and `probe.go`,
783	   `SetBasicAuth` only in `nexusapi.go`, and `net/http/httputil` is imported
784	   nowhere. Comments are not read. Limit: a header name built by concatenation,
785	   or a whole `http.Header` printed with `%v`, is not seen.
786	
787	**The mise guard** (`mise_tasks_test.go`) reads `mise.toml` with a small
788	line-based reader (no TOML library in `go.mod`) and checks: the six tasks exist
789	and call the command; none of `ci`, `check`, `test`, `test-race` reaches a
790	`nexus-bench` task, directly or through `depends` and `run` references; `kubectl`
791	is declared on `up`, `provision`, `down`, `status` and `test`, absent on `render`
792	and absent from the global `[tools]`; `nexus-bench:test` sets
793	`DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1`, runs `-run Integration` and carries a `-timeout` of at
794	least 45 minutes. Limit: it reads the file, it does not ask mise to resolve it.

22	## Vision et stratégie (décision de stratégie proposée à l'utilisateur, non contredite)
23	
24	Aujourd'hui DevDesk parle à Nexus de deux façons, et **aucune n'a été mesurée sur un Nexus
25	reproductible** : l'API REST de gestion (`/service/rest/v1/*`, découverte des membres d'un
26	groupe) et l'API Docker Registry v2 que Nexus sert (`_catalog`, `tags/list`). Le contrat OpenAPI
27	de Nexus suffit à écrire clients, types et faux serveurs pour la première ; il ne dit **rien** du
28	comportement de la seconde, qui porte toutes les hypothèses ouvertes (R1 d'image-search, IS-16).
29	
30	Stratégie : (1) construire un banc Nexus jetable, **déployé uniquement sur le cluster k0s de la
31	machine `datomir`** (décision du 2026-11-16), reproductible sans accès à l'entreprise ;
32	(2) **mesurer** dessus les hypothèses 1-4 ; (3) rejouer ces mesures comme fixtures de test
33	(réponses réelles enregistrées, plus des fixtures écrites depuis un contrat) ; (4) corriger ce que
34	les mesures contredisent ; (5) retirer les mentions « non validé sur registre réel ». L'instance
35	de l'entreprise est un **complément facultatif**, jamais un prérequis.

48	Le banc Nexus tourne **uniquement** sur la machine `datomir`, dans le cluster k0s qui y tourne déjà.
49	On n'installe ni Docker ni Podman pour lui (Docker peut perturber le réseau des pods d'un nœud k0s ;
50	k0s embarque déjà containerd). **Pas de repli local en conteneur.** Les tests et les mesures tournent

56	  `datomir` (192.168.1.31). Les tests joignent donc Nexus par `127.0.0.1` ou `192.168.1.31`, via
57	  des Services NodePort : plus de question d'accès réseau entre deux machines.

130	
131	- **Le banc est coupé en deux** (NX-01 instance + comptes + dépôts ; NX-02 peuplement +
132	  scénarios commutables) : un seul bloc serait un L et mélangerait deux capacités vérifiables
133	  séparément (une instance qui démarre et se provisionne ; un jeu de données et un amont qu'on
134	  peut couper à la demande).
135	- **Les hypothèses sont mesurées en trois stories** (NX-03 `_catalog` + droits + hôte partagé ;
136	  NX-04 « cached only » ; NX-05 routage, realm, redirections, `Link`) : trois questions
137	  indépendantes, parallélisables, qui ne s'envoient pas la même correction.
138	- **Le routage par chemin et par port est fusionné dans NX-05** (mesure) au lieu d'être une story
139	  de développement séparée : le modèle `(url, repo_prefix)` couvre déjà les quatre modes
140	  (`registries.md`, D39/§3.18) ; sans mesure il n'y a pas de capacité nouvelle à livrer. Si la
141	  mesure en révèle une, elle devient une story (section « Corrections conditionnelles »).
142	- **Le durcissement du client REST (NX-06) ne dépend pas du banc** : tout est vérifié sur le code
143	  et testable en `httptest`. Il peut partir en parallèle de NX-01.
144	- **« Corrections issues des mesures » n'est pas une story** : sa taille est inconnue avant NX-03
145	  à NX-05 (INVEST : non estimable). Elle est listée en section dédiée, non créée dans Plane.
146	- **Ajoutées** : NX-07 (refus vs vide dans la découverte, défaut V4), NX-08 (fixtures enregistrées),
147	  NX-09 (« cached only » par membre proxy, fruit de H3), NX-10 (recherche par l'API de recherche
148	  de Nexus, repli si `_catalog` est refusé), NX-11 (alignement de la documentation, clôture d'IS-16).
149	- **Retirée** : une story « lister toutes les repositories d'une instance pour proposer une case
150	  par proxy ». Elle élargit le périmètre sans besoin exprimé (la demande du 2026-08-10, une case
151	  par proxy, est servie par la déclaration `kind: registry` + `repo_prefix`) ; elle est reprise

194	## Epic — Support complet de Nexus
195	
196	**Objectif** : mesurer sur un Nexus reproductible ce que DevDesk n'a jamais vu d'un vrai Nexus,
197	durcir le client REST, corriger ce que les mesures contredisent, et retirer les mentions « non
198	validé sur registre réel ». Dans Plane, l'epic est un **module** (les types de work item, donc les
199	epics natifs, ne sont pas disponibles en édition Community, voir les conventions Plane) ; les
200	stories y sont rattachées, sans `parent`.

365	### NX-02 — Le banc contient des images connues et un amont qu'on peut couper
366	Epic : Support complet de Nexus — Priorité : Must (validé) — Effort : **M** (PM, à confirmer ; était S) — Dépend de NX-01
367	
368	En tant que mainteneur, je veux que le banc soit peuplé de jeux de données déterministes et que je
369	puisse rendre l'amont d'un proxy injoignable afin de rejouer les scénarios « hosted », « proxy
370	rempli », « proxy vide », « amont coupé » et « groupe ».
371	
372	**Critères d'acceptation**
373	1. Étant donné le banc provisionné (NX-01), quand le peuplement s'exécute depuis la machine de dev,
374	   alors le dépôt hosted reçoit au moins trois images (dont un nom à un composant, `api`, et un nom à
375	   deux, `team/api`) avec des tags connus, par un **client sans démon** (`skopeo`, présent sur l'hôte ;
376	   `crane`, absent : choix à confirmer) et **jamais par le client Docker** ; le registre étant servi en
377	   **HTTP**, le client est lancé avec la vérification TLS désactivée explicitement (ex.
378	   `--dest-tls-verify=false` pour skopeo, `--insecure` pour crane), pour les adresses du banc seulement.
379	2. Étant donné le proxy, alors son amont est un **second registre jetable déployé dans le même
380	   namespace** (Deployment et Service, image de registre minimale tirée de Docker Hub, **jamais du
381	   préfixe `tvp-zot.incus:5000`**, et jamais d'image du banc poussée dans ce zot), joignable par le proxy
382	   sous son nom de Service, **jamais Internet** pour le trafic du proxy ; son contenu est alimenté
383	   depuis la machine de dev par le même client sans démon.
384	3. Étant donné le proxy et l'amont, quand une image n'a été tirée qu'à travers le proxy (copie vers un
385	   répertoire local par le client), alors le proxy la contient en cache ; une seconde image présente
386	   seulement dans l'amont reste **absente du cache** (jeu de données « partiellement en cache »).
387	4. Étant donné le banc peuplé, quand je coupe l'amont (commande dédiée : **le Deployment de l'amont
388	   passe à 0 réplica**), alors les images déjà en cache restent servies par le proxy et les autres
389	   échouent ; quand je le rétablis (**retour à 1 réplica**, la commande attend qu'il soit prêt), elles
390	   redeviennent disponibles **avec le contenu de l'amont d'avant la coupure**.
391	5. Étant donné le groupe, alors il contient le hosted et le proxy ; une image n'existe que dans l'un
392	   d'eux, une autre dans les deux (cas de doublon).
393	6. Étant donné un peuplement relancé, alors le résultat est identique (idempotent) ; le descripteur de
394	   NX-01 est complété avec les noms d'images et de tags attendus et le mode d'accès (HTTP).
395	7. Étant donné le banc, alors une commande de remise à zéro rend le jeu de données à son état
396	   initial **sans recréer l'instance** (ni le namespace, ni le pod Nexus).

461	questions ouvertes du document).
462	
463	---
464	
465	### NX-04 — Mesurer ce qu'un proxy Nexus liste quand son amont est coupé (« cached only »)
466	Epic : Support complet de Nexus — Priorité : Should — Effort : S (PM, à confirmer) — Dépend de NX-02
467	
468	En tant que mainteneur, je veux mesurer ce qu'un proxy et un groupe mixte listent réellement afin
469	de savoir si la mention `Cached only` (IS-14, `listsCacheOnly`) est exacte, trop large ou fausse.
470	
471	Story de **mesure** (spike), même format que NX-03.
472	
473	**Critères d'acceptation**
474	1. Étant donné le proxy avec l'amont joignable et une image **non** encore en cache, quand on
475	   demande `tags/list` puis `_catalog`, alors le rapport note si l'image absente du cache est
476	   listée, tirable, ou ni l'une ni l'autre (H3).
477	2. Étant donné l'amont coupé (NX-02) et une image en cache, alors le rapport note ce que renvoient
478	   `tags/list` et `_catalog` : liste du cache, erreur, ou vide, avec les codes HTTP.
479	3. Étant donné le groupe mixte (hosted + proxy, NX-02), alors le rapport note, **par membre**, si
480	   `_catalog` et `tags/list` listent ensemble le hosted et le cache du proxy, et si un nom en double
481	   apparaît deux fois.
482	4. Étant donné ces réponses, alors le rapport dit quel verdict DevDesk affiche aujourd'hui pour
483	   chacun (`ok`, `no result`, `refused`, `failed`, mention `Cached only`) en jouant les cas par les
484	   fonctions de classification existantes sur les réponses enregistrées, et conclut : mention exacte,
485	   trop large (hosted marqué à tort), ou insuffisante.
486	5. Étant donné la conclusion, alors elle est classée confirmée, contredite ou non concluante pour
487	   H3, et alimente NX-09.
488	
489	**Hors périmètre** : changer la règle de la mention (NX-09) ; mesurer `_catalog` (NX-03).
490	**Faits** : Vérifié sur le code : la mention se décide par `config.IsNexusGroup` et `listsCacheOnly`
491	(un membre de groupe, proxy ou hosted indifféremment, Q7 d'image-search) ; la source du comportement
492	« limité au cache » est secondaire (`research.md`, `network.md` : « not verified on a real Nexus »).
493	À valider sur instance : H3.
494	**Questions ouvertes** : aucune.
495	
496	---
497	
498	### NX-05 — Mesurer routage par chemin et par port, realm Bearer, redirections et pagination
499	Epic : Support complet de Nexus — Priorité : Should — Effort : M (PM, à confirmer) — Dépend de NX-02
500	
501	En tant que mainteneur, je veux mesurer comment un Nexus réel se laisse atteindre (chemin,
502	connecteur de port, sous-domaine), comment il authentifie et s'il redirige afin de savoir ce que le
503	modèle `(url, repo_prefix)` et la règle « aucune redirection hors origine » (D142) supportent vraiment.
504	
505	Story de **mesure** (spike), même format que NX-03 ; elle fusionne « routage par chemin » et
506	« routage par port » car le modèle `(url, repo_prefix)` couvre déjà les deux (voir décisions de
507	découpage).
508	
509	**Critères d'acceptation**
510	1. Étant donné trois dépôts du banc joignables respectivement par chemin (`/v2/<dépôt>/…`), par
511	   connecteur HTTP dédié (`docker.httpPort`, exposé par un Service NodePort hors des ports déjà pris,
512	   voir D2) et, si le DNS le permet, par sous-domaine (règles Traefik, voir D7), quand `tags/list` est demandé par le client de DevDesk avec l'URL et le
513	   `repo_prefix` documentés pour chaque mode (`registries.md`), alors le rapport note le résultat de
514	   chaque mode (200, 404, 401, erreur de schéma `http://`).
515	2. Étant donné un `401`, alors le rapport note le défi `WWW-Authenticate` (Basic ou Bearer), l'**URL
516	   du realm** et si elle est **sur la même origine** que le registre, avec le Docker Bearer Token
517	   Realm actif puis désactivé.
518	3. Étant donné chaque mode, alors le rapport note si un redirect est émis (tags, `_catalog`,
519	   manifest, blob) et vers quelle origine ; un redirect hors origine est signalé comme **impraticable
520	   avec le client actuel** (D142) sans avoir été suivi.
521	4. Étant donné un `_catalog` ou `tags/list` plus grand que la page demandée (assez d'images pour
522	   paginer), alors le rapport note la forme de `Link` (URL relative/absolue, même origine) et si
523	   `n=` est respecté.
524	5. Étant donné le compte administrateur, le compte « pull » et l'accès anonyme, alors le rapport
525	   note pour chaque mode lequel de ces trois accès fonctionne (périmètre d'authentification).
526	6. Étant donné les mesures, alors chaque point de H4 est classé confirmé, contredit ou non
527	   concluant, avec les réponses brutes expurgées conservées pour NX-08.
528	
529	**Hors périmètre** : corriger le code ; pull effectif d'une image par un moteur de conteneurs (le pull
530	n'est pas le travail du client HTTP de DevDesk, et un registre HTTP distant demande une déclaration
531	« insecure », R-NX6) ; reverse proxy externe devant Nexus (cas de l'entreprise) ; installer un
532	contrôleur d'Ingress sur `datomir` (Traefik existe déjà ; une ressource Ingress ou IngressRoute dans le
533	namespace du banc, elle, est dans le périmètre).
534	**Faits** : Vérifié sur le code : `registryAPIURL` accepte `http://`, `https://` et `host:port` ;
535	`refuseOffOriginRedirect` et `sameOrigin` refusent tout redirect ou `Link` hors origine. Vérifié sur
536	`datomir` (2026-11-16, D7) : une IngressClass `traefik` existe (par défaut, namespace `traefik`) : le
537	routage par chemin est faisable avec Traefik ; NodePorts déjà pris à éviter : 30300, 30880, 30881, 30891
538	à 30895, 30903, 31930 (D2) **[liste incomplète, remplacée le 2026-11-16 : 30080 et 30890 sont aussi pris ; l'outil relit les Services du cluster ; connecteurs de NX-05 dans le bloc réservé 30483-30489, voir « Constaté » de NX-01]**. À valider sur instance : H4 en entier ; Hypothèse: le realm Bearer d'un
539	Nexus peut pointer une URL d'une autre origine derrière un reverse proxy, ce que le banc ne reproduit
540	que si une règle Traefik le met en situation. Hypothèse: chaque connecteur Docker de Nexus
541	(`docker.httpPort`) demande un port de Service distinct (un NodePort libre par connecteur).
542	Hypothèse: le routage par chemin est servi par le port HTTP principal de Nexus, avec ou sans Traefik
543	(à mesurer). Hypothèse: les règles de Traefik, ses points d'entrée, son TLS et ses certificats sont
544	inconnus ; sans eux, le banc est servi en HTTP et le comportement en HTTPS (certificats, realm sur une
545	origine TLS) n'est pas mesuré. Hypothèse: un DNS pour des sous-domaines n'est pas disponible (non
546	relevé).
547	**Questions ouvertes** : règles de Traefik, points d'entrée, TLS et DNS pour sous-domaines (existence de
548	l'Ingress tranchée, D7) ; authentification à couvrir (voir questions ouvertes du document).
549	
550	---
551	
552	### NX-06 — Le client REST de Nexus ne suit pas une redirection hors origine, borne sa lecture et type ses erreurs
553	Epic : Support complet de Nexus — Priorité : Must — Effort : S (PM, à confirmer) — Aucune dépendance
554	
555	En tant qu'utilisateur qui enregistre un compte Nexus, je veux que l'appel à l'API de gestion se
556	comporte comme celui du registre (D142) afin qu'un serveur ou un lien piégé ne reçoive ni mes
557	identifiants, ni une réponse géante, et que les refus soient distinguables.
558	
559	**Critères d'acceptation**
560	1. Étant donné un serveur de test qui répond `302` vers une **autre origine** (schéma, hôte ou
561	   port différent), quand la découverte d'un groupe est lancée, alors la requête s'arrête avec une
562	   erreur qui ne contient ni chemin ni requête de la cible, aucune requête n'est émise vers
563	   l'autre origine, et aucun en-tête `Authorization` n'y est envoyé.
564	2. Étant donné une réponse dont le corps dépasse la borne (1 Mio proposé, comme le jeton de D142),
565	   quand elle est lue, alors la lecture s'arrête et l'appel échoue avec une erreur explicite ; un
566	   corps tronqué n'est **jamais** décodé comme un succès.
567	3. Étant donné une réponse 401, 403, 404, 429 ou 5xx, quand l'appel échoue, alors l'erreur expose
568	   son code HTTP (récupérable par `errors.As`) et la source (API de gestion) ; le message ne contient
569	   ni identifiant ni mot de passe.
570	4. Étant donné une échéance dépassée ou une annulation du `context`, alors l'erreur le dit
571	   (`errors.Is` sur `context.DeadlineExceeded` / `context.Canceled`) et n'est pas confondue avec une
572	   erreur HTTP.
573	5. Étant donné les appelants actuels (`DetectGroup`, `fetchRepoMeta`, `fetchGroupMembers`), alors
574	   leurs tests existants passent, et un redirect **sur la même origine** reste suivi.
575	6. Étant donné un serveur de test qui renvoie un corps `JSON` invalide ou vide, alors l'erreur le
576	   dit sans panique et sans décoder partiellement.
577	
578	**Hors périmètre** : le défaut V4 (erreurs avalées par `fetchGroupMembers`, NX-07) ; les deux autres
579	points que D142 a laissés (`internal/oci/oci.go:46`, `internal/ui/oci_resources/commands.go:412`),
580	à traiter à part ; pagination (V5 : le code ne lit qu'un dépôt à la fois).
581	**Faits** : Vérifié sur le code : V1 (aucun `CheckRedirect`, `nexus.go:28`, `:203`), V2 (`io.ReadAll`
582	non borné, `nexus.go:212`), V3 (erreur `HTTP %d` non typée, `nexus.go:209`) ; `internal/oci` possède
583	déjà le modèle à suivre (`refuseOffOriginRedirect`, `StatusError`, `maxTokenResponse`). À valider sur
584	instance : rien.
585	**Hypothèses** : Hypothèse: la borne de 1 Mio suffit pour une réponse `/v1/repositories/{nom}` d'un
586	groupe de plusieurs centaines de membres ; à vérifier sur le banc ou l'instance (négociable).
587	Hypothèse: réutiliser le code d'`internal/oci` plutôt que le dupliquer ne crée pas de dépendance
588	circulaire avec `registrymgr` (choix technique laissé à l'architect).
589	**Questions ouvertes** : aucune.
590	
591	---
592	
593	### NX-07 — Un groupe dont les membres sont refusés n'est pas pris pour un groupe vide
594	Epic : Support complet de Nexus — Priorité : Should — Effort : M (PM, à confirmer) — Dépend de NX-06
595	
596	En tant qu'utilisateur d'un groupe Nexus avec un compte de pull, je veux savoir si la liste des
597	membres est vide, refusée ou illisible afin de ne pas croire qu'un groupe n'a pas de membre alors
598	que Nexus a refusé de me le dire.
599	
600	**Critères d'acceptation**
601	1. Étant donné un faux Nexus dont `/v1/repositories/<nom>` répond « group » sans `memberNames` et
602	   dont `/v1/repositories/docker/group/<nom>` répond 403 (compte de pull), quand la découverte
603	   s'exécute, alors le résultat distingue « membres **refusés** » de « 0 membre » : il porte la
604	   cause, récupérable par `errors.Is`/`errors.As`, et n'est **pas** mis en cache comme un groupe
605	   sans membre.
606	2. Étant donné le même faux Nexus avec un second appel `200` et `memberNames` vide, alors le
607	   résultat est « 0 membre », mis en cache comme réponse réglée.
608	3. Étant donné une erreur réseau ou une échéance sur le second point, alors le résultat est « non
609	   joignable » (erreur propagée), distinct du refus, et rien n'est écrit dans le cache (cohérent
610	   avec D23).
611	4. Étant donné un refus, alors l'interface (onglet Registries / en-tête) dit en anglais que les
612	   membres n'ont pas pu être lus avec ce compte et qu'ils peuvent être déclarés à la main avec
613	   `repo_prefix` ; aucun `err.Error()` brut n'est affiché.
614	5. Étant donné les membres déjà déclarés à la main pour ce groupe, alors ils continuent de
615	   fonctionner et ne sont pas masqués par le refus.
616	6. Étant donné les entrées déjà en cache avant la correction (groupe mis en cache sans membre),
617	   alors elles sont retraitées comme « inconnues » à la prochaine ouverture, sans migration
618	   manuelle.
619	
620	**Hors périmètre** : le durcissement HTTP (NX-06) ; lister tous les dépôts d'une instance (retiré,
621	voir décisions) ; la forme exacte de l'affichage (négociable avec l'UX).
622	**Faits** : Vérifié sur le code : V4 (`fetchGroupMembers` avale toute erreur et `DetectGroup` rend
623	`members, nil`, `nexus.go:75-77`, `:121-148`), l'appelant décide de la mise en cache de `nil, nil`
624	(D23). À valider sur instance : que Nexus répond bien **403** (et non 404 ou une liste vide) sur le
625	point détaillé pour un compte de pull (mesuré le 2026-08-10 sur l'instance de l'entreprise, à
626	reproduire sur le banc, NX-03 critère 3).
627	**Questions ouvertes** : libellé et emplacement du message (négociable, à valider avec l'UX).
628	
629	---
630	
631	### NX-08 — Les réponses réelles de Nexus enregistrées servent de tests de régression
632	Epic : Support complet de Nexus — Priorité : Should — Effort : S (PM, à confirmer) — Dépend de NX-03, NX-04, NX-05
633	
634	En tant que mainteneur, je veux que les tests de recherche et de découverte rejouent des réponses
635	**mesurées** sur le banc (expurgées) plutôt que des réponses écrites à la main afin qu'une

637	
638	**Critères d'acceptation**
639	1. Étant donné les réponses brutes de NX-03 à NX-05, quand elles sont versées dans le dépôt, alors
640	   chacune est expurgée (aucun secret, aucun nom interne), porte la version de Nexus et le scénario

642	2. Étant donné ces fixtures, quand les tests de `internal/imagesearch` et `internal/registrymgr`

1	# The Nexus bench — `internal/nexusbench`
2	
3	> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
4	> read this file when working on the code it describes.
5	
6	## What it is
7	
8	DEVDESK-504 (NX-01): a disposable Nexus Community instance on the k0s cluster
9	of `datomir`, deployed, provisioned over REST and destroyed with one command, so
10	the registry measurements of the NX stories run against a real Nexus. It is a
11	development tool: the `dk` binary does not import it, nothing in `mise run
12	check` or `mise run ci` touches a cluster, and integration tests skip unless
13	`DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1` is set (and always when `CI` is set).
14	
15	Status: the parameters (step 1), the manifest rendering (step 2), the `kubectl`
16	runner, errors and preflight (step 3), the deployment and its wait (step 4), the
17	secrets store and the descriptor (step 5), the REST client and provisioning
18	(step 6), the destruction (step 7), the command with its mise tasks (step 8) and
19	the guarded integration tests with the source guards (step 9) exist. The
20	preflight only reads the cluster; the writes are the two applies of `Deploy`,
21	the REST calls of `Provision` and the namespace delete of `Destroy`.
22	
23	Validated on `datomir` on 2026-11-16 (step 10, see "First real run" below): `up`,
24	a second `up`, the three read-only integration tests and the destructive
25	lifecycle all ran against a real Nexus 3.98.1-01 Community on k0s. One
26	hypothesis was wrong (a proxy whose upstream does not resolve is refused), and
27	`Provision` now copes with it.
28	
29	## Decisions (plan `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-504-plan.md`)
30	
31	- **D-A** A Go package, `internal/nexusbench`, with a `package main` under
32	  `cmd/nexus-bench`, driven by `mise run nexus-bench:*` tasks outside `ci`.
33	  `kubectl` through `os/exec`, no `client-go`, no bash.
34	- **D-B** Namespace `nexus-bench`, context `datomir`, NodePorts 30481 (REST,
35	  UI) and 30482 (Docker connector); 30483-30489 reserved for the next NX
36	  stories. Refused: namespaces `default`, `kube-*`, `app-*`, `flux-system`,
37	  `local-path-storage`, `traefik`, `kyverno`, `observability`, `plane`; NodePorts
38	  outside 30000-32767 or equal; an image from `tvp-zot.incus:5000` (Kyverno
39	  `verify-tvp-images` admits signed images only).
40	- **D-C** Resources 500m/2 CPU, 3Gi/4Gi memory, 5Gi PVC, JVM 1 GiB heap and 1 GiB
41	  direct memory, image `docker.io/sonatype/nexus3:3.98.1`. To be confirmed on
42	  the first real run (H-RES).
43	- **D-D** A deterministic, versioned `descriptor.json` (no timestamp, pod name or
44	  secret); secrets in a `0600` file outside the repository, shared by all
45	  worktrees.
46	- **D-E** Idempotent REST provisioning: read, then create or replace; admin
47	  password changed with the new one written first; the EULA is accepted only
48	  with `NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA=yes`.
49	- **D-F** One typed error with a cause and a check to run; the preflight runs
50	  before any write; the namespace carries a `managed-by` label and `down`
51	  refuses to delete one without it.
52	
53	## Parameters (`params.go`)
54	
55	Precedence: flag, then `NEXUS_BENCH_*` variable, then default. `FromEnv(base,
56	getenv)` applies the variables onto `base` and returns a new value (the base is
57	not changed); an empty variable counts as unset; a value that does not parse is
58	an error naming its variable. `Validate()` runs before any call to the cluster
59	and reports every problem at once. Every value that reaches a manifest is
60	checked against a strict pattern, newlines included. The patterns are meant to
61	keep a value from injecting YAML on their own, but the templates still
62	writes every value quoted: the validation is the first guard, not the only one.
63	
64	| Field | Variable | Default |
65	|---|---|---|
66	| `Context` | `NEXUS_BENCH_CONTEXT` | `datomir` |
67	| `Namespace` | `NEXUS_BENCH_NAMESPACE` | `nexus-bench` |
68	| `HTTPNodePort` | `NEXUS_BENCH_HTTP_NODEPORT` | `30481` |
69	| `DockerNodePort` | `NEXUS_BENCH_DOCKER_NODEPORT` | `30482` |
70	| `CPURequest` / `CPULimit` | `NEXUS_BENCH_CPU_REQUEST` / `_CPU_LIMIT` | `500m` / `2` |
71	| `MemoryRequest` / `MemoryLimit` | `NEXUS_BENCH_MEMORY_REQUEST` / `_MEMORY_LIMIT` | `3Gi` / `4Gi` |
72	| `StorageSize` | `NEXUS_BENCH_STORAGE_SIZE` | `5Gi` |
73	| `JVMOpts` | `NEXUS_BENCH_JVM_OPTS` | `-Xms1g -Xmx1g -XX:MaxDirectMemorySize=1g -Djava.util.prefs.userRoot=/nexus-data/javaprefs` |
74	| `Image`, `ImageTag` | `NEXUS_BENCH_IMAGE`, `_IMAGE_TAG` | `docker.io/sonatype/nexus3`, `3.98.1` |
75	| `UpstreamURL` | `NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL` | `http://bench-upstream.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:5000` |
76	| `Anonymous` | `NEXUS_BENCH_ANONYMOUS` | `true` |
77	| `AcceptEULA` | `NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA` | `false`; true only for the exact value `yes` |
78	| `Hosts` | `NEXUS_BENCH_HOSTS` (comma list) | none: derived (`127.0.0.1`, node InternalIP) |
79	| `Timeout`, `DeleteTimeout` | `NEXUS_BENCH_TIMEOUT`, `_DELETE_TIMEOUT` | `10m`, `3m` |
80	| `SecretsPath`, `DescriptorPath` | `NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`, `NEXUS_BENCH_DESCRIPTOR` | none: derived |
81	
82	Rules beyond the shape of each value:
83	
84	- CPU, memory and storage quantities are greater than zero (`0`, `0m`, `0Gi` are
85	  refused), and a request never exceeds its limit (CPU compared in milli-cores,
86	  memory in bytes, units mixed freely: `2000m` equals `2`). The error names both
87	  variables, so a lone `NEXUS_BENCH_MEMORY_LIMIT=2Gi` against the default `3Gi`
88	  request is refused.
89	- `JVMOpts` is 1-512 characters among letters, digits, space and `_ . , : = / + @ %
90	  -`; it starts with a letter, a digit, or `-` followed by a non-space (so not
91	  `- x`, `@x`, `%x`, `,x`, `:x`), holds no `": "` and does not end with `:`, so it is
92	  a plain YAML scalar by itself.
93	- `Hosts` entries are IP addresses or host names (letters, digits, `.`, `-`,
94	  253 characters at most): no port, no whitespace.
95	- `UpstreamURL` is `http://` or `https://` plus a host, without credentials, made
96	  of URL characters only (no `@`, no whitespace) and with a port, when present,
97	  between 1 and 65535.
98	- Paths hold no control character and are 4096 bytes at most.
99	
100	`NEXUS_BENCH_NAMESPACE` alone moves `UpstreamURL` to the new namespace, unless
101	the base already carried a custom upstream or `NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL` is set.
102	The context name is limited to letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `@` and `-`, because
103	it names a directory of the secrets path.
104	
105	## Manifests (`render.go`, `manifests/`)
106	
107	`Render(p Params) ([]byte, error)` calls `p.Validate()` first (an invalid value
108	returns Validate's error, naming its variable, and no bytes) and writes a
109	multi-document YAML stream separated by `---`, in this order: Namespace, PVC,
110	Deployment, Service. `RenderNamespace(p)` returns the first document alone, so
111	that `up` can apply the Namespace before the rest. The output is deterministic
112	(no map iteration, no timestamp); the golden of the defaults is
113	`testdata/render-default.golden.yaml`, rewritten with
114	`go test ./internal/nexusbench -run TestRenderGolden -update` and reviewed as a
115	diff.
116	
117	| File (`go:embed`, `text/template`) | Object |
118	|---|---|
119	| `00-namespace.yaml.tmpl` | Namespace, labels `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by` and `part-of` = `devdesk-nexus-bench`; no `pod-security.kubernetes.io/*` label |
120	| `10-pvc.yaml.tmpl` | PVC `nexus-data`, `ReadWriteOnce`, `StorageSize`, no `storageClassName` (the cluster default class, `local-path`) |
121	| `20-deployment.yaml.tmpl` | Deployment `nexus`: 1 replica, `Recreate`, one container (`ImageRef`), ports `http` 8081 and `docker-group` 8082, requests and limits, env `INSTALL4J_ADD_VM_PARAMS`, PVC on `/nexus-data`, `startupProbe` on `/service/rest/v1/status` (10 s x 60 = 10 min), `readinessProbe` (same path), no `livenessProbe`, UID and GID 200, `runAsNonRoot`, no privilege escalation, `drop: [ALL]`, `RuntimeDefault` seccomp, no service account token, no service links |
122	| `30-service.yaml.tmpl` | Service `nexus`, `NodePort`: `http` 8081 to `HTTPNodePort`, `docker-group` 8082 to `DockerNodePort` |
123	
124	Quoting: the templates see only a `manifestData` built from validated values,
125	and every string goes through the `q` template function (`strconv.Quote`, a
126	valid YAML double-quoted scalar), so `true`, `null`, `123`, `0x1F`, `12:30:45` or
127	`2001-01-23` in `NEXUS_BENCH_JVM_OPTS` decode as strings (`TestRenderRoundTripsTrickyJVMOpts`,
128	`TestRenderQuotesEveryValue`). Quoted: namespace, image reference, JVM options,
129	CPU and memory quantities, storage size. Not quoted: the two NodePorts (integers),
130	and the literals of the template (names, labels, container ports).
131	
132	What the render does not carry: the context, the upstream URL, `Anonymous`,
133	`AcceptEULA`, `Hosts`, timeouts and paths (a change of any of them leaves the
134	bytes unchanged, `TestRenderIgnoresParamsTheManifestsDoNotCarry`); no Secret, no
135	ConfigMap, no `envFrom` or `valueFrom`, no hostPath, no object of cluster scope
136	but the Namespace; the word `password` or `secret` never appears. The admin
137	password is read from the pod and written to the secrets file by the
138	provisioning step, not by a manifest.

140	## Errors, runner and preflight (`errors.go`, `kubectl.go`, `preflight.go`)
141	
142	**Errors.** Every failure of the bench is a `*BenchError{Kind, Cause, Check, Err}`.
143	`Error()` is `"<Cause>. Check: <Check>"`: a probable cause and what to run or look
144	at (a `kubectl` command, or a `mise` task), in English. `Err` is kept for
145	`errors.Is`/`errors.As` and is never printed: the text of a failed sub-process can
146	carry a credential, and neither the stderr of kubectl nor its error reaches a
147	message. `ErrKind` holds the kinds of D-F in the order the bench meets them:
148	`KubectlMissing`, `ContextNotFound`, `ClusterUnreachable`, `Forbidden`,
149	`NamespaceForeign`, `NamespaceMissing`, `NodePortTaken`, `AdmissionDenied`,
150	`PodPending`, `ImagePull`, `Crash`, `Deadline`, `RESTUnreachable`,
151	`ProvisionFailed`. The zero value is `Unclassified`, so an error nobody classified
152	never passes for a named kind. The last six are for the steps to come.
153	
154	`classifyKubectl(stderr)` is the fallback for what the exit status and the JSON
155	cannot tell apart; kubectl's wording changes between versions, so it matches
156	lower-cased fragments and returns `Unclassified` for an unknown text. Order of the
157	rules: an admission webhook that denied (even reported as `Forbidden`) is
158	`AdmissionDenied`; `provided port is already allocated` or `... not in the valid
159	range` is `NodePortTaken`; `forbidden` is `Forbidden`; `Unable to connect to the
160	server`, `connection refused`, `i/o timeout`, `TLS handshake timeout` are
161	`ClusterUnreachable`.
162	
163	**Runner.** `Runner.Run(ctx, stdin, args...)` returns both streams even on
164	failure. `NewExecRunner(context)` finds `kubectl` with `exec.LookPath` (a
165	`KubectlMissing` error otherwise, which names `kubectl` and `mise install`) and
166	puts `--context <context>` before every call, so callers never pass it.
167	`kubectl.go` is the only non-test file of the package that starts `kubectl`; the one other process is the `git check-ignore` of the secrets store (see below).
168	
169	**Preflight.** `RunPreflight(ctx, r, p, op) (PreflightResult, error)` with `op` one
170	of `OpUp`, `OpProvision`, `OpDown`, `OpStatus`. Checks, in this order, stopping at
171	the first failure:
172	
173	1. `p.Validate()`: invalid parameters are refused before any call.
174	2. `kubectl config get-contexts -o name`: the exact context name is listed, else
175	   `ContextNotFound`. Nothing else is asked.
176	3. `kubectl get --raw /readyz`: the API server answers, else `ClusterUnreachable`;
177	   a refusal (stderr `forbidden`: expired token, 403) is `Forbidden` instead, through
178	   the same `classifyKubectl` as every other call.
179	4. `kubectl auth can-i <verb> <resource>` (`-n <ns>`, `-A` or nothing):
180	   `up` needs create and patch `namespaces` (cluster; a server-side apply is a
181	   PATCH, also on a second run), create `persistentvolumeclaims`, `services`,
182	   `deployments` and `pods/exec` (namespace), list `services` (`-A`),
183	   patch `deployments`, `services` and `persistentvolumeclaims`, and get and list
184	   `pods` and `persistentvolumeclaims` (the wait of `Deploy`), all in the
185	   namespace (no manifest creates a Secret, so none is asked);
186	   `provision` needs create `pods/exec`, get `deployments` and list `pods`
187	   (namespace); `down` needs delete `namespaces`; `status`
188	   asks nothing. A `no` arrives on stdout with a non-zero exit, so stdout is read
189	   first: `Forbidden`, naming the verb and the resource.
190	5. `kubectl get namespace <ns> -o json`: absent is fine for `up` and `down` (nothing
191	   to delete) and `NamespaceMissing` for `provision` and `status`; present
192	   without the label `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=devdesk-nexus-bench` is
193	   `NamespaceForeign` for every operation (the plan lists `up` and `down`;
194	   `provision` and `status` refuse too, so the bench never runs `exec` in a
195	   namespace it did not create).
196	6. `up` only, `kubectl get services -A -o json`: a Service other than `nexus` of
197	   our namespace that holds `HTTPNodePort` or `DockerNodePort` is `NodePortTaken`,
198	   naming `<namespace>/<name>` and the port. Our own Service is accepted, which is
199	   what makes a second `up` possible.
200	7. Everything but `down`, `kubectl get nodes -o json`: `NodeIP` is the first
201	   `InternalIP`; none is not an error (`NodeIP` stays empty).
202	
203	A call that fails in a way the checks above did not expect goes through
204	`classifyKubectl` (a `forbidden` stderr becomes `Forbidden`, anything unknown
205	`Unclassified`). Every call that reaches the API server carries
206	`--request-timeout=10s`.
207	
208	**No write before the end of the preflight.** The preflight issues `config`,
209	`get` and `auth can-i` only, never sends stdin, and a failure at any point leaves
210	the cluster untouched. The tests run it against a scripted fake runner that fails
211	the test on any call outside the six above and records every write verb
212	(`apply`, `create`, `delete`, `patch`, `exec`, ...) it would have seen. The
213	`Runner` of the later steps (apply, delete) is only called after `RunPreflight`
214	returned without an error.
